headline: Scotland mandates swift bricks in new buildings to save declining bird
meta_description: Scotland becomes first UK nation to require swift bricks in all new buildings, tackling a 70% decline in swift populations since the 1990s.
summary_short: Scotland has become the first UK nation to mandate swift bricks in all new buildings—a landmark conservation step addressing a dramatic 70% decline.
body:
Scotland has become the first UK nation to mandate swift bricks in all new buildings, marking a landmark step to help reverse a 70% decline in swift numbers since the 1990s.

Swift populations have faced relentless pressure as modern construction and renovation removes the gaps and cavities these birds depend on for nesting. By requiring swift bricks—specially designed nesting chambers built into new structures—Scotland is shifting from passive decline to active restoration at the building level.

The mandate transforms construction standards themselves into a tool for species recovery. Rather than treating bird conservation as separate from development, this policy weaves it directly into the built environment, creating potential nesting habitat wherever new buildings rise across the nation.
quick_facts: Scotland is the first UK nation with this mandate
Requirement applies to all new buildings
Swift bricks are specially designed nesting chambers
